author: SamuelBrudner
text: 2026-10-26 live diagnosis and product requirement: the user says nobody will open the app without an inbox ping and explicitly selected the connected Yale Outlook account for automated review emails. Primary app has drafting scheduler/background enabled, review_email_enabled=true, transport=external, no SMTP configuration. Three accounts and three personal notification routes are present and enabled. There are 18 assigned READY batch reviews; 15 have any outbox row, three have none. Last provider acceptance was 2026-08-13. Initial unaccepted rows: pending=1, retryable=7, failed=4; two failed rows intentionally suppressed and must not be replayed. Two other rows have transport_unavailable with very high historical attempt counts. Verified the documented bare docker exec claim fails after leasing because entrypoint-exported signing key is absent. Correct invocation adds -e LAB_TRACKER_AUTH_SECRET_KEY_FILE=/app/data/runtime-env/auth-secret-key. A real claim for the user rendered a signed fixed cue; Sent lookup found no duplicate; Outlook send returned HTTP 403 ErrorAccessDenied, so no email was sent. Recorded that lease as authentication_rejected, and released the earlier preparation-failure lease with a sanitized terminal error. User has been asked to reconnect Outlook with sending permission; no unattended sender was enabled while send is denied. lab-tracker-ja73 fixes preflight/leasing and documents the correct command. Keep this delivery issue open until a real send, Sent confirmation, outbox acknowledgement, and unattended subsequent run succeed; then recover missed reviews with current routing, preserve intentionally suppressed rows and deduplication, and avoid flooding each inbox with historical per-review messages.
